clue.text: Heath backtracking on rubbish before s spreads rapidly

parts.note: mush is soft pulp, here taken as nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: backtracking says the word for heath is read backwards

parts.note: a moor is open heathland
the letter s as printed

explanation.surface: Some plant on rotten ground ahead of an s-shaped growth, like weeds taking over a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' looks like a noun here, but the definition is a verb phrase; the lone 's' is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mushroom is a verb meaning to grow or expand very fast, like fungi popping up overnight.

clue.text: Tremendous leg-over, I see

indicators.note: over, in a down clue, says the word for leg is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: gam is slang for a leg
the letter C is pronounced 'see'

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast about a night's 'leg-over', with a knowing 'I see' in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg-over' is British slang for sex, but the hyphen hides a split: a word for leg, then 'over' to turn it up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is informal British praise meaning wonderful or excellent.

clue.text: Cleaner takes bogus waste

parts.note: sham means fake or bogus
poo is bodily waste

explanation.surface: A cleaner who pockets fake rubbish while working.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap used for washing hair or carpets, so a cleaning product.

clue.text: Honourably pay butler for working

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: An employer decently paying the butler for his labour.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputably means in a way that has a good reputation, i.e. respectably or with honour.

clue.text: Male in public display behind where the cow went?

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
he is the male pronoun
to moon is to display one's bare behind

explanation.surface: A man exposing himself in public, then a nursery-rhyme cow.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Hey Diddle Diddle' the cow jumped over the moon; the phrase also means delighted.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery rhyme cow's leap carried her above the lunar disc, so that phrase names her destination.

clue.text: Note pulled-up short stockings

indicators.note: pulled-up, in a down clue, means the letters are read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: hose is a word for stockings

explanation.surface: Pulling up stockings that are too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts HOSE to HOS, and 'pulled-up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Soh is the fifth degree of the sol-fa musical scale, a single note.

clue.text: Pick up tropical disease possessed by solver

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: yaws is a tropical skin infection

explanation.surface: A warning about catching a tropical illness that the reader already has.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent YAWS and YOURS sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Yours is the possessive pronoun for the person addressed, and the clue addresses the solver.

clue.text: Sing up in party hosted by diocese

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says everything is read backwards
hosted by means the party goes inside the diocese

parts.note: Ely is an English cathedral city and diocese
do is a party

explanation.surface: Singing out at a church party in the diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire that gives its name to a diocese; yodle is an accepted variant spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodle, a variant of yodel, is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Relating to one college Rector banned from lounge

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college

indicators.note: banned from means the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: to tarry is to linger or lounge about

explanation.surface: A college rector being barred from the common lounge.
explanation.definitionFit: Unitary describes something forming a single whole unit, so pertaining to oneness.

clue.text: Genuinely past joining bank

parts.note: since means ago, in the past
to bank on is to rely

explanation.surface: Someone sincerely recalling having once joined a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincerely means honestly, without pretence.

clue.text: Grip core of mangrove fruit

indicators.note: the core is the centre, so the middle letters of the word are taken

parts.note: the middle two letters of mangrove
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Taking hold of fruit from the heart of a mangrove swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' plays on an apple's core.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to seize and wrestle with, i.e. take a firm hold.

clue.text: Guy from Rome once owned and managed island breaks

parts.note: had means possessed or owned

indicators.note: the island breaks into the words, splitting them

parts.note: ran means managed

explanation.surface: A man of ancient Rome who once ran an island estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is not the name Guy but simply a man, and 'once' marks him as historical.
explanation.definitionFit: Hadrian was a Roman emperor, the builder of the famous wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Get into trouble screwing with PC?

parts.note: a PC, police constable, is a cop
it is slang for sex, i.e. screwing

explanation.surface: Fiddling with a personal computer and landing in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a computer, but it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cop it is British slang meaning to be punished or get into serious trouble.

clue.text: Perhaps service water sports around western island

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go on either side
sports is used in the sense of shows off in a new form, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the word water as printed

indicators.note: western, in an across clue, means going westward, so read right to left

parts.note: Elba is a Mediterranean island

explanation.surface: Water sports taking place around an island in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water sports' reads as one phrase, but 'sports' is the anagram signal acting on 'water'; Elba is Napoleon's island of exile.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner or tea service is a set of plates and cups, an example of crockery for the table.

clue.text: Woody nightshade is better with wet ground

indicators.note: ground, as in milled or crushed, means the letters are broken and reformed

explanation.surface: Gardening advice that a nightshade does best in wet soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Bittersweet is the common name of the climbing plant Solanum dulcamara.

clue.text: Leading characters in William of Orange's court

indicators.note: the leading characters of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Something set in the royal court of William of Orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a noun for the royal household, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to pursue them romantically.

clue.text: Rowers etc. developed as City material?

indicators.note: developed means changed into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rowers and others growing into city-firm material.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcester is a cathedral city in England and also the name of a fine woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an English city and a type of worsted fabric, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Test betrayal she concocted

indicators.note: concocted means made up or cooked up, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A woman inventing a treacherous test.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathalyse is to check a driver's breath for alcohol, a roadside examination.

clue.text: Drags arse about — that's concerning

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dragging their backside around, which is a worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concerning' sounds like worrying but means 'about the matter of'.
explanation.definitionFit: As regards is a phrase meaning with reference to, on the subject of.

clue.text: Off-the-shelf book, perhaps two starting in several months?

parts.note: a book is something one may read

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for months

parts.note: a year is a stretch of twelve months

indicators.note: starting, as in jumping with surprise, signals the letters are jolted into a new order

parts.note: the word two as printed

explanation.surface: A book where two characters set off over the course of a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starting' is used in the sense of jumping in surprise, so it jumbles 'two'; 'several months' is loose but fair for a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-wear clothes are made in standard sizes and sold finished, not tailored.

clue.text: Pleasantness ain't my bent when covering base

indicators.note: covering means the rearranged letters go around the base
bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in maths

explanation.surface: A grumble that pleasantness isn't someone's inclination when covering for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Amenity can mean the quality of being agreeable, i.e. pleasantness, as well as a facility.

clue.text: Nothing aboard extremely heavy boat

indicators.note: aboard means the zero is placed inside
extremely means taking the letters at the extremes, first and last

parts.note: the first and last letters of heavy
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A heavily laden boat with nothing on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel once used for carrying goods and passengers.

clue.text: Artiste formerly in international couple beginning to hurry up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the string is read from the bottom

parts.note: the word in as printed
a duo is a couple

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of hurry

explanation.surface: A former performer in a double act, told to get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, I, DUO and H make INIDUOH, which 'up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was a celebrated escapologist and stage illusionist of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Football legend backing county's top performers, the greatest?

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Pelé was the great Brazilian footballer
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A football great supporting a county's star players.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire is a county in southern England, abbreviated HANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants were the star attractions of the circus, billed as the greatest show on earth, and are the largest land animals.

clue.text: For some, religiously legitimate passage contains answer

indicators.note: contains means the word holds the letter within it

parts.note: a hall is an entrance passage

explanation.surface: A religious text in which a legitimate passage contains the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Halal describes what is permitted under Islamic law, especially meat, so lawful to Muslims.

clue.text: Punishment once held back in justifiable urgency

indicators.note: held back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the answer lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A former punishment that was delayed despite a justified need to act fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unused; it is the signal that the letters are concealed in 'justifiable urgency'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone their gruel was an old idiom for punishing or killing them.

clue.text: Both hands holding a hollow globe — it's huge

indicators.note: holding means the pair of letters goes around the next

parts.note: L and R for left and right hands

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: outer letters of globe

explanation.surface: Someone cradling a hollow globe in both hands, marvelling at its size.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means big, of considerable size.

clue.text: Observe where to go in temporary shelter

parts.note: to twig is to notice or realise
the loo is where one goes, a toilet

explanation.surface: Noting the toilet's location inside a makeshift shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: A loo is a British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A twigloo is a makeshift hut of branches built by road protesters, a pun on igloo.

clue.text: Oscar's AC/DC fetish

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, BI

explanation.surface: Oscar's fetish for the rock band AC/DC.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the band but is slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi, also obeah, is a West Indian form of sorcery, and also a charm or fetish used in it.

clue.text: Facetiously more noble in days of yore

definitions.meaning: jokingly, more like an earl, the comparative of an invented adjective
at a previous time, before now

explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the word as earl plus the comparative ending.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary sense is at a former time; the jokey one treats it as an earl-like comparative.

clue.text: Sail ahead of, on occasion, standard navy marines we commission

definitions.meaning: a small sail set above the topgallant

definitions.text: ahead of, on occasion, standard navy marines we commission
definitions.meaning: the word goes in front of each of these: the ... Standard, ... Navy, ... Marines, ... we and ... Commission

explanation.walkthrough: The royal we is the monarch's use of 'we' for 'I'; the others are British institutions or the monarch's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigger the royal is a high sail; the second sense is the adjective prefixing each regal title.

clue.text: Stupid, missing as crossing river or section of canal

indicators.note: crossing means the river goes across the middle of the word
missing means those letters are left out

parts.note: asinine means stupid, like an ass
the word as printed
the Test is a river in Hampshire

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly failing to cross a river by a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a famous trout river in Hampshire, southern England; 'canal' means the alimentary canal, not a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: The intestine is part of the alimentary canal, the gut running through the body.
